key_insight: MANTA lets a multi-agent system adapt its communication topology during inference, so collaboration can self-evolve when the current organization is no longer effective.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to more robust agent orchestration by updating roles, links, order, visibility, and validation without changing the task interface or agent budget.
method: Initialize a task-conditioned communication topology from prior structural experience.
Monitor collaboration traces during execution and apply bounded structural updates when needed.
Adjust agent roles, communication links, execution order, information visibility, and validation pathways.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmarks spanning information seeking, tool use, planning, workflow execution, and mathematical reasoning, MANTA achieved the highest average score of 74.0, beating the strongest baseline by 5.8 points and ranking best on PlanCraft.
watch_item: Adaptive topology updates may add runtime complexity and require careful safeguards to avoid destabilizing coordination or overfitting structural changes to specific tasks.
paper_title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
